question: arXiv:1410.3696v1 derives the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray background with three reference foreground models, A, B and C. Why do the authors go beyond the class of Galactic diffuse emission models studied before, to which model A belongs, and in what do models B and C differ from model A?

arguments.answer:
Why: Model A comes from the class of GALPROP DGE models in Ackermann et al. 2012, which covered only a limited set of propagation/injection scenarios. They assumed a constant diffusion coefficient throughout the Galaxy, and the same source population injecting electrons and nuclei. The authors show (Appendix A) that IC templates from such models are inconsistent in the multi-component likelihood fit. For example, the predicted IC spectrum does not match the spectrum fitted to the LAT data. That matters because the isotropic template could partly compensate for a wrong IC distribution and bias the IGRB. So they add two reference models with more degrees of freedom, to test whether the IGRB spectral features depend on the foreground model.

Differences from A: Model A has CR nuclei and electrons injected by sources tracing the pulsar distribution, with a constant diffusion coefficient and re-acceleration strength. Model B adds a separate electron-only source population near the Galactic center, which produces most of the IC emission. It also needs a local source of soft electrons to explain the electron spectrum below 20 GV. Model C keeps a single source population, but it is more centrally peaked than the pulsar distribution. Its diffusion coefficient and re-acceleration strength vary with Galactocentric radius and height above the plane.
